newsitem.title: SOUTH AFRICA: TARIFFS ON S.AFRICAN WATER TO RISE FROM APRIL 1.
newsitem.headline: TARIFFS ON S.AFRICAN WATER TO RISE FROM APRIL 1.

text.p: South African Water Affairs and Forestry Minister Kader Asmal said on Monday tariffs on water from government schemes would be raised from April 1 to cover higher operating and catchment management costs.
The ministry said in a statement the new tariffs, which will be published in the Government Gazette early in March, would generally show increases of lower than 10 cents per cubic metre.
However, where "special circumstances" prevailed, such as in the Vaal River system, the average annual increase would be 23.5 cents per cubic metre.

Asmal said price increases, which were in line with policies approved by the cabinet in February last year, were aimed at the recovery of the full financial costs of government water schemes supplying water for urban and industrial use.

He said proposed increases in tariffs on water for irrigation tallied with agreements reached with the South African Agricultural Union early in 1996 and should therefore not be damaging to that sector.

Asmal said the price moves were necessary to ensure a smooth transition towards realistic pricing of water in South Africa. A new water pricing policy is presently being developed which will culminate in a final White Paper towards the end of the year.
